o.text: Borrowed from Classical Persian مُوَفَّقِیَّت (muwaffaqiyyat). By surface analysis, müvəffəq + -iyyət.
From Old Anatolian Turkish شول (şol), from earlier اوش اول (uş ol), the latter part corresponding to Azerbaijani o (“he, she; that”). Compare Turkmen şol.
From dodaqlan- (“to be pronounced by means of the lips”) + -ma (“negative verbal suffix”) + -yan (“subject non-past participle suffix”). Calque of Russian неогублённые (neogubljónnyje).
